items.text: Ex-Formula One chief Bernie Ecclestone won’t go to prison after confessing to tax fraud in the UK. He admitted misleading the British tax authority about assets worth over 492 million dollars. Ecclestone will pay a total of 803 million dollars in tax, interest, and penalties for 18 tax years between 1994 and 2022. He pleaded guilty to fraud by giving false information in 2015 when he denied being the beneficiary of various trusts, including one that transferred more than 500 million dollars to a Singapore bank account in 2010. The judge handed him a 17-month suspended prison sentence, meaning he’d serve jail time only if he committed another crime within two years. Difficult words: fraud (the crime of obtaining money or property by deceiving people), plea d (to make a statement of what you believe to be true), beneficiary (a person who receives money or assets from a trust, will, or insurance policy). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ex-Formula One boss Bernie Ecclestone doesn’t have to go to jail after he admitted tax fraud . He said sorry for not telling the truth about his overseas assets worth over 492 million dollars. He will pay 803 million dollars in tax, interest , and penalties for 18 tax years from 1994 to 2022. The 92-year-old said that he lied to the tax authority in 2015 when he claimed that he didn’t own some assets, including one that sent 500 million dollars to a Singapore bank account in 2010. The judge gave Ecclestone a 17-month suspended prison sentence, which means that he will only go to jail if he breaks the law within two years. Difficult words: tax fraud (when a person or organization cheats in order not to pay taxes), asset (something what a person or company owns), interest (money which someone has to pay for the use of money lent or for a delayed payment). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bernie Ecclestone is an ex-Formula One boss. Ecclestone does something wrong in 2015. He says that some things do not belong to him. But this is not true. These things are in other countries. They are worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Ecclestone does not want to pay high taxes. Ecclestone pays little taxes between 1994 and 2022. Now, he must pay 803 million dollars. He says that he is sorry for not telling the truth about his money. The judge says that Ecclestone does not have to go to jail if he does nothing bad for two years. Difficult words: worth (how much something costs), tax (money which people and companies pay to the government), jail (a place where people who do something bad stay for some time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After a year in power, Italy’s far-right prime minister Giorgia Meloni hasn’t fulfilled her promise to halt illegal migration. However, she’s become influential in Europe’s immigration discussions. Italy is a key location for migration to Europe, and the numbers have been increasing. If EU leaders don’t find solutions, Meloni plans to use the immigration issue to gain support for her far-right allies in the upcoming EU elections. Over time, she has shed some of her controversial image and gained popularity for bringing stability, even among left-leaning individuals. However, her transformation remains unclear to many. Meloni has adopted a more pragmatic stance in Europe, supporting Ukraine and advocating for deals in Africa, including immigration issues. She has formed new international relationships, including with Joe Biden and Volodymyr Zelenskiy, while also deepening ties with far-right allies like Viktor Orbán in Hungary. Difficult words: halt (to stop), controversial (causing disagreement and discussion), stance (how someone stands on an issue). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Italy’s far-right prime minister Giorgia Meloni got to power one year ago. She promised to deal with illegal migration from Africa, but she failed. Italy is an important destination for people who are coming to Europe, and their numbers are growing. If EU leaders don’t find a solution, Meloni plans to use the migration topic to get support in the EU elections. Meloni is not as controversial as she was a year ago. She became more popular because she made Italy a more stable country. Yet, many people don’t believe this change. Meloni supports Ukraine and pushes for deals in Africa. She built new relationships with leaders like Joe Biden and Volodymyr Zelenskiy. But she also got closer to far-right Viktor Orbán from Hungary. Difficult words: far-right (a person or political party with extreme ideas and views), controversial (making people argue and disagree), stable (calm and not changing so very much). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Giorgia Meloni is the prime minister of Italy. She has far-right ideas. A year ago, Meloni says that she will stop illegal migration from Africa. It does not happen. But Meloni is now an important person in Europe when talking about migration. Italy is a place where many people come to Europe. And more people are coming every year. It can happen that leaders in Europe will not agree on what to do about migration. If so, Meloni wants to use this situation to be successful in the European elections . Some people think that she is not as strict as in the past. Even people who do not agree with her ideas like her more. She makes Italy more stable. Meloni is friends with Joe Biden or Volodymyr Zelenskiy, but she is also getting closer to far-right Viktor Orbán in Hungary. Difficult words: far-right (extreme and not liking big changes), migration (when people come to live and work in another country), elections (when people vote for someone or for a group of people to do a job in politics). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two Lockheed Martin F-35A fighter jets have made history by landing on a motorway, as seen in Norwegian military footage. This capability allows the jets to minimize their time on the ground during wartime, enhancing their survivability. The aircrafts that belong to the Royal Norwegian Air Forc, landed in Tervo, Finland, as part of a military exercise. After landing, they underwent hotpit refuelling where engines remained running. Major General Rolf Folland, chief of the Royal Norwegian Air Force, emphasized the importance of using small airfields and motorways to protect fighter jets from ground vulnerabilities in times of conflict. Finland, which shares a long border with Russia and recently joined NATO, plans to purchase 64 F-35 fighter jets from Lockheed Martin. Difficult words: enhance (to increase or further improve something), vulnerability (the quality of being easily hurt or influenced). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Two Lockheed Martin F-35A fighter jets did something special – they landed on a highway. This could help them be safer during a war. The planes belong to the Royal Norwegian Air Force and they landed in Tervo, Finland. They got fuel while their engines were running. This is called hotpit refuelling. Major General Rolf Folland, the leader of the Royal Norwegian Air Force, said that fighter jets are not safe when they are on the ground. So, using small airfields and now motorways makes them safer during a war. Finland is close to Russia and the two countries share a long border. Finland is newly part of NATO and it wants to buy 64 F-35 fighter jets. Difficult words: fighter jet (a fast military plane), fuel (petrol for planes), airfield (an area of land where planes take off and land). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two special planes land on a highway . They are fighter jets from Norway. It is part of a training. It happened in Tervo, Finland. The planes get fuel while their engines are working. This is called hotpit refuelling. This makes the planes safer during a war. The leader of the Norwegian Air Force says that fighter planes are not safe when they are on the ground. So, landing on roads is good for them. They do not need fields. They can take off and land more easily. Finland is close to Russia. They have a long border together. Finland wants to buy 64 of these planes. Difficult words: highway (a fast road), fighter jet (a fast plane which soldiers use), fuel (a substance which planes need to fly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A prisoner swap between Iran and the United States is set to occur alongside the transfer of $6 billion in unfrozen Iranian funds to banks in Qatar. This carefully orchestrated exchange will see detained US dual nationals released from Iran and Iranian prisoners in the US returning home. The process began with Iran releasing four US citizens into house arrest on August 10, followed by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken hinting at their eventual return. The negotiation, mediated by Qatar, bypasses the contentious US-Iran nuclear dispute. Qatar will oversee the funds’ usage to ensure compliance with US sanctions. Once the funds reach Qatar, American prisoners will fly to Qatar from Tehran, and Iranian prisoners will return to Iran from the US. This unexpected cooperation follows a period of strained relations between the two nations. Difficult words: orchestrated (carefully planned and organized), dual national (a person who is a national of two countries at the same time), contentious (causing or likely to cause an argument). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Iran and the United States will exchange prisoners soon, and they will also move $6 billion to banks in Qatar. First, Iran released four US citizens from prison on August 10. The US Secretary of State said that this was the start of a process to send them home. The people released include 51-year-old Siamak Namazi, 59-year-old Emad Sharqi, and Morad Tahbaz who is 67. Tahbaz also has British citizenship . The US didn’t say who the other two people were. Qatar helped Iran and the US talk and made the swap happen. Qatar will also make sure that Iran spends the money the right way. When Qatar receives the money, it will tell Iran and the US to release the prisoners. Difficult words: release (to set free), citizenship (when someone is a national of a country), swap (exchange). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iran and the United States will exchange prisoners soon. They will also send $6 billion to Qatar’s banks. This will happen next week. Iran lets four US people out of prison on August 10. The US Secretary of State says this is the first step to send them home. The US does not say who the prisoners are. Some of them have dual citizenship . It means that they can officially live in two countries, Iran and the United States. Qatar helps Iran and the US talk and make the exchange happen. Qatar will also make sure Iran uses the money the right way. Qatar will tell Iran and the US when to let the prisoners go. Difficult words: exchange (to give a thing and get another thing), prisoner (a person who does something bad and he or she must stay in a special place), citizenship (when someone can officially stay and live in a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
